**Answer: 16**

**Upper bound.** Let $C$ be the set of cells of one colour. Every cell in $C$ has at least two orthogonal neighbours in $C$, so the subgraph of the grid induced on $C$ has minimum degree at least 2. A finite graph with minimum degree at least 2 contains a cycle. The grid is bipartite, so every cycle has even length, and the shortest cycle in the grid is the 4-cycle formed by a $2\times 2$ block. Hence $|C| \ge 4$.

Since the board has 64 squares and each colour class has at least 4 squares, there are at most $64/4 = 16$ colours.

**Construction.** Divide the $8\times 8$ board into sixteen disjoint $2\times 2$ blocks and give each block its own colour. Every square then has exactly two orthogonal neighbours in its block, both of its own colour, so the condition holds. This uses 16 colours.

Therefore the maximum is 16.

ANSWER: 16
